ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #19
====

GRADE: Grade 1
SUBJECT: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Harmful effects of? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Harmful effects of.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Harmful effects of.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Harmful effects of.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Harmful effects of.

3. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

4. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. joule (J)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. newton (N)

5. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

6. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 37 °C

7. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Milk souring
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Iron rusting

8. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Tertiary consumers
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Producers

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Uses of water? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Uses of water.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Uses of water.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Uses of water.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Uses of water.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Plants its resources? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Plants its resources.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Plants its resources.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Plants its resources.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Plants its resources.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Sounds that alert us? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Sounds that alert us.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Sounds that alert us.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Sounds that alert us.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Sounds that alert us.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Energy resources? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Energy resources.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Energy resources.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Energy resources.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Energy resources.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Caring for plants environment and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Caring for animals environment and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Managing waste environment and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Safety in handling and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:

====

1. B — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

2. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Harmful effects of.

3. A — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

4. D — newton (N)

5. D — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

6. C — 100 °C

7. A — Ice melting to water

8. D — Producers

9. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Uses of water.

10. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Plants its resources.

11. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Sounds that alert us.

12. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Energy resources.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Caring for plants environment; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
